es: Escribir un relato breve con narrador en primera persona, tiempos narrativos variados (pasado simple, continuo y perfecto), un símil y una oración enfática, y crear atmósfera con detalles que preparan lo que vendrá.

teaching.en: The narrator tells the story and uses the opening lines to set the scene, so the reader knows where and when everything happens.
teaching.es: El narrador cuenta la historia y usa las primeras líneas para crear el escenario, de modo que el lector sepa dónde y cuándo ocurre todo.
teaching.explanationEs: El narrador suele usar el pasado; el escenario pide pasado continuo y la acción puntual, pasado simple.

the scene, so the reader knows where and when everything happens.

teaching.en: It was raining when I reached the deserted station, and a single lamp was shining over the empty platform.
teaching.es: Llovía cuando llegué a la estación desierta, y una sola lámpara brillaba sobre el andén vacío.
teaching.explanationEs: Past continuous (was raining, was shining) para el escenario; past simple (reached) para la acción puntual.
segments: It was raining when I reached the deserted station, and
a single lamp was shining over the empty platform.
teaching.audioText: It was raining when I reached the deserted station, and a single lamp was shining over the empty platform.

teaching.en: When I arrived, the last train had already left, which made the eerie silence of the platform feel even heavier.
teaching.es: Cuando llegué, el último tren ya había salido, lo que hizo que el inquietante silencio del andén pesara aún más.
teaching.explanationEs: Past perfect (had left): algo que pasó antes de otro momento del pasado; eerie crea atmósfera.
segments: When I arrived, the last train had already left, which
made the eerie silence of the platform feel even heavier.
teaching.audioText: When I arrived, the last train had already left, which made the eerie silence of the platform feel even heavier.

teaching.en: The silence between us was like a wall, and the smell of wet stone made the night feel even colder.
teaching.es: El silencio entre nosotros era como un muro, y el olor a piedra mojada hacía que la noche pareciera aún más fría.
teaching.explanationEs: Un símil con like da una imagen; un detalle de olor o de sonido hace la escena más vívida.
segments: The silence between us was like a wall, and the
smell of wet stone made the night feel even colder.
teaching.audioText: The silence between us was like a wall, and the smell of wet stone made the night feel even colder.

teaching.en: What I remember most is the smell of rain on the platform, because that was the moment I understood that I was alone.
teaching.es: Lo que más recuerdo es el olor a lluvia en el andén, porque fue el momento en que comprendí que estaba sola.
teaching.explanationEs: What + oración + is: énfasis en lo que quieres destacar.
segments: What I remember most is the smell of rain on the platform,
because that was the moment I understood that I was alone.
teaching.audioText: What I remember most is the smell of rain on the platform, because that was the moment I understood that I was alone.

teaching.en: It was the old key that opened the door, and this small detail seemed to foreshadow the secret that the story would reveal later.
teaching.es: Fue la vieja llave la que abrió la puerta, y este pequeño detalle parecía anticipar el secreto que la historia revelaría después.
teaching.explanationEs: It was + cosa + that/who: énfasis en quién o qué hizo la acción; foreshadow = dejar pistas de lo que vendrá.

prompt.es: Elige la frase correcta sobre algo que ocurrió antes.

choices.text: When Leo reached the platform, the last train has already left.

When Leo reached the platform, the last train was already leaving.

feedback.es: Had + participio (had already left) marca que el tren salió antes de la llegada de Leo; las otras opciones no respetan esa secuencia.

hint.es: Lo anterior a otro momento del pasado usa had + participio.

origin.text: Narrator's notes: Leo reached the platform at ten past nine. The last train left at nine.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del relato con su función.

pairs: She opened the letter and froze.
He had lost his keys long before.

feedback.es: Was getting dark pinta el escenario, opened es la acción, had lost es lo anterior y like a bright light es un símil.

prompt.es: Escucha el comienzo del relato y elige qué había ocurrido antes de llegar la narradora.

choices.text: She had found a key on the bench.
Her phone had lost its signal.

feedback.es: «The last train had already left» indica que el tren salió antes de que ella llegara; la llave y el teléfono aparecen después.

origin.audio: It was getting dark when I reached the deserted station, and the platform smelled of wet stone. The last train had already left, and the silence felt like a wall between me and the rest of the city. I took out my phone, but it had no signal. Then I noticed a small key on the bench, with a red label. It was the label that caught my eye, because my grandmother used to put one just like it on each of her keys.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que enfatiza lo que más recuerda el narrador.

choices.text: What I remember most is the smell of the bakery.
I remember most what is the smell of the bakery.
It is the smell of the bakery what I remember most.

feedback.es: What I remember most is… es la estructura enfática correcta; «es el olor lo que recuerdo» no se copia palabra por palabra del español.

origin.text: The narrator wants to stress the smell of the bakery, not the noise of the street outside.

prompt.es: Elige la versión con los tiempos narrativos adecuados.

It was snowing while I waited, when a stranger appeared at the gate.
It had snowed while I waited, when a stranger appears at the gate.

feedback.es: El escenario (nevaba) va en pasado continuo y la aparición del desconocido, una acción puntual, en pasado simple.

origin.text: Opening of a story: the narrator wants to describe the weather while she waits, and then report the moment when a stranger appeared at the gate.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué ocurrió antes de que Leo llegara a casa.

choices.text: He had made some tea for his sister.
The family had left the house.
His sister had gone to bed.

feedback.es: «Had already gone to bed» sitúa el acostarse de la hermana antes de la llegada de Leo; el té lo prepara después.

origin.audio: When Leo reached the house, the lights were off and his sister had already gone to bed. He made some tea and sat in the kitchen without a sound, because he did not want to wake her. It was her coat that he noticed first, still wet by the door, although she had told the whole family that she would stay in all evening.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué sugiere el detalle del abrigo mojado.

choices.text: That his sister had been out, despite saying she would stay in.
That rain had blown in through a window his sister left open.
That the family had been out together earlier that evening.

feedback.es: El abrigo mojado prueba que salió bajo la lluvia, aunque había dicho que se quedaría en casa: el detalle anticipa un secreto.

prompt.es: Escribe el relato: dos tiempos narrativos, un símil y una oración enfática.

answer.text: It was raining when I reached the deserted station, and my bag was heavy. I had promised Sara that I would be there at eight, but the last train had already left. A man was sleeping on a bench, and a small clock was showing the wrong time above the ticket office. I felt cold and afraid. What I remember most is the silence, which was like a wall between me and the rest of the city. I took out my phone, but it had no power. Then I heard a voice behind me. It was my old teacher who was standing there with an umbrella! She had seen me from the bus and had followed me inside. She laughed, gave me her phone and said, “Call Sara. She has probably been waiting for you.” I called, and Sara answered at once. She was not angry. In fact, she had missed the train too, and she was waiting at the next station. We met her an hour later, and we laughed about the whole night. I will never forget how kind both of them were.
accepted: It was raining when I reached the deserted station, and my bag was heavy. I had promised Sara that I would be there at eight, but the last train had already left. A man was sleeping on a bench, and a small clock was showing the wrong time above the ticket office. I felt cold and afraid. What I remember most is the silence, which was like a wall between me and the rest of the city. I took out my phone, but it had no power. Then I heard a voice behind me. It was my old teacher who was standing there with an umbrella! She had seen me from the bus and had followed me inside. She laughed, gave me her phone and said, “Call Sara. She has probably been waiting for you.” I called, and Sara answered at once. She was not angry. In fact, she had missed the train too, and she was waiting at the next station. We met her an hour later, and we laughed about the whole night. I will never forget how kind both of them were.

It was getting dark when I arrived at the cinema, and a long line was waiting outside. I had bought the tickets two days before, but when I looked in my bag, I understood that I had left them at home. My heart was beating like a drum. What I felt most was shame, because Leo had already told everyone that the film was his idea. I walked to the desk and explained the problem. The woman smiled and said, “Do not worry. Show me the message on your phone.” I looked for it, but my hands were shaking. Finally I found it. It was a small miracle that the message was still there! She checked the name, printed two new tickets and wished us a good film. When I found Leo, the film had already started, so we sat in the dark and whispered like children. Afterwards we walked home and he laughed at me all the way. I remember that night as the day I learned to check my bag twice.

feedback.es: Un buen relato usa el continuo para el escenario, el pasado simple para la acción, el perfecto para lo anterior, un símil con like o as y una oración enfática.

origin.text: Escribe un relato en primera persona de 200 a 250 palabras sobre una noche en que llegaste tarde a un lugar importante (una estación, un cine, una fiesta). Usa al menos dos tiempos narrativos (por ejemplo, past continuous para el escenario y past perfect para lo anterior), un símil con like o as, una oración enfática (What… is… o It was… who/that…) y un detalle que anticipe lo que vendrá.

it was a small miracle that

prompt.es: ¿Qué efecto crea la frase «My footsteps sounded like a slow clock»?

choices.text: A metaphor that turns the narrator into a slow clock.
A simile that makes the steps sound slow and tense.
A personification that gives the old clock a voice.

feedback.es: Like a slow clock compara los pasos con un reloj: es un símil, y junto con el ritmo de la narradora transmite nerviosismo y tensión.

origin.text: The station was empty, and the clock above the platform had stopped at midnight. My footsteps sounded like a slow clock, and I walked faster, because I felt that someone was watching me from the dark.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué recuerda más la narradora.

choices.text: The sound of the heavy rain.
The moment she lost her keys.
The silence of the empty street.

feedback.es: «What I remember most is the silence of the street» enfatiza el silencio, no la lluvia ni las llaves.

origin.audio: When she called, I had already left home, so I missed the first ring. By the time I reached the corner, it was raining hard, and I realised that I had forgotten my keys. What I remember most is the silence of the street, which was like a held breath.
